system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Rust (reading the book)
G2: Go (did the tour)
G3: machine learning (unfinished course)
G4: AWS certification (course only, no exam)
G5: Terraform authoring
G6: official team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Copying the 'Learning: Rust, Go' line as skills
T2: Turning the unfinished AWS Cloud Practitioner course into a certification or the unfinished ML course into ML skills
T3: Calling him Tech Lead / Team Lead as a job title (project tech lead only; acting lead only in notes)
T4: Claiming Terraform authoring
T5: Failing to condense: keeping duplicated Älvgrind sections, hobbies, gymnasium, band
T6: Dropping qualifiers like 'Vue (a little)', 'Tailwind (some)'
T7: Old cover letter is to his current employer and says he is at Sjöbris

# OUTPUT 1: CV
OSKAR
Senior Full-Stack / Frontend Engineer
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior full-stack engineer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications.
Strongest in frontend development with React and TypeScript, with hands-on experience building
Node.js services and working with PostgreSQL. Experienced in onboarding and identity-verification
features, secure document workflows, and leading delivery on a customer-facing mobile app. Also served
as acting team lead for four months in 2024.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, React Native, Angular
Backend: Node.js, NestJS, Express, GraphQL, Apollo Server
Databases and data: PostgreSQL, TypeORM, Prisma
Cloud and messaging: AWS ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS, Firebase Cloud Messaging
Other: Laravel, WordPress, Terraform (small edits), Python (basic), YAML
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Fullstack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB 2021–Present
• Build onboarding features using React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS.
• Delivered a Swedish BankID identity-verification step supporting QR-code and same-device flows
through a provider SDK. A/B tested with 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion
increased from 61% to 74%.
• Implemented a secure ID-document upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV virus scanning in
Lambda, SQS status updates and PostgreSQL.
• Contributed to an incremental migration of the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, moving
route by route behind the same API gateway.
• Maintained a backend-for-frontend (BFF) using Apollo Server and GraphQL.
• Served as acting team lead for four months in 2024 during the team lead’s parental leave, including
1:1s and sprint planning.
Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB 2018–2021
• Delivered web and mobile projects for agency clients using Angular, React, React Native, Laravel
and WordPress.
• Tech lead and primary app developer for a ferry-ticket mobile application, working in a two-developer
team. Built the React Native and TypeScript app for purchasing and showing tickets offline; the
other developer handled the payment backend. The app reached approximately 50,000 downloads.
Developer | Nordkust Media 2014–2018
• Worked on newspaper websites.
SELECTED PROJECTS
Express to NestJS Migration | Älvgrind Fintech 2021–2022
• Helped migrate the onboarding backend incrementally from Express to NestJS, route by route,
behind the same API gateway.
• Gave a meetup talk about the migration in 2022.
• Technologies: Node.js, Express, NestJS, TypeORM, Prisma.
BankID Identity Verification Flow | Älvgrind Fintech 2022
• Built a new onboarding identity step using Swedish BankID, including QR-code and same-device
flows through a provider SDK.
• A/B tested on 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
• Technologies: React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS ECS.
Secure Document Upload | Älvgrind Fintech 2023
• Built an ID-document upload flow supporting files up to 20 MB, with S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV
virus scanning in Lambda, and scan-status updates through SQS into PostgreSQL.
• Technologies: AWS S3, Lambda, SQS, NestJS, PostgreSQL.
Ferry Ticket Mobile App | Sjöbris Digital, for a ferry operator 2019–2020
• Led the technical delivery and built most of a React Native app for buying and showing ferry tickets
offline. The app reached approximately 50,000 downloads.
• Technologies: React Native, TypeScript, Node.js, Firebase Cloud Messaging.
PERSONAL PROJECTS
Home Assistant Integrations | 2022–Present
• Built two small custom home-automation integrations, published on GitHub with approximately 40
stars combined.
• Technologies: Python (basic), YAML

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Verdane Care team,
I have 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications. Since 2021, I’ve
worked on onboarding features at Älvgrind Fintech using React, TypeScript, NestJS and
PostgreSQL. My strongest area is frontend development, and I also bring hands-on experience
building Node.js services with NestJS and Express, working with PostgreSQL, and handling
data-sensitive workflows.
A project especially relevant to Verdane Care’s patient-facing work is an identity-verification
step using Swedish BankID, with both QR-code and same-device flows. We tested it with 10%
of traffic before rollout, and onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%. I also built a
secure ID-document upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, virus scanning and status updates.
These projects gave me practical experience building important user journeys in a
privacy-sensitive fintech context, with identity verification, secure document handling, and
careful protection of personal information.
I’m drawn to Verdane Care’s focus on making healthcare feel more human, and to principles
such as “Patients first” and “Privacy by default.” Earlier in my career, I led the technical
delivery and built most of a React Native ferry-ticket app for purchasing and showing tickets
offline; it reached approximately 50,000 downloads. That experience strengthened my interest in
building useful, dependable experiences for people using mobile products.
I’d welcome the opportunity to bring my React and TypeScript experience, Node.js and
PostgreSQL backend background, and experience building user-facing features to the Patient
Experience team. Thank you for considering my application.
Best regards,
Oskar

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
